passage:
The principal's room was cold from the air conditioner. Lokesh stood in front of Principal Vidya's desk. His phone was in her drawer, taken because he was said to have used it in class. It was not true, he had only been checking the time for the exam bell.
His first instinct was to say, "This is so unfair, you never listen!" He could feel the words in his mouth. Instead he took a breath. "Ma'am, may I explain? I'd like to say what happened, and then you can decide."
Vidya folded her hands. "Go on."
He told her about the exam clock. She nodded and said, "I'll check with your teacher."

qa.q: Where did Lokesh's phone end up after the incident?
qa.a: Lokesh's phone was in Principal Vidya's drawer.

qa.q: What was Lokesh feeling as he stood in front of the principal's desk, choosing his words?
qa.a: Lokesh felt indignant and worried about the unfairness. Holding back "this is so unfair" shows he wanted to be heard, not to fight.

qa.q: What did Lokesh choose to say, and what did it change?
qa.a: Lokesh said, "Ma'am, may I explain?" and offered to describe what happened. Vidya folded her hands, listened and promised to check with his teacher.

qa.q: How might Principal Vidya have reacted if Lokesh had said "you never listen"?
qa.a: Vidya would probably have felt challenged and the talk would have turned into a power fight. Instead she listened and agreed to check.

grounding: A teenager who feels unfairly treated speaks to a principal with respectful directness, "may I explain", rather than rudeness.

passage:
"Papa, you said no without even listening!" Uday said, slamming his bag on the sofa.
Gautam looked up from the newspaper. "Watch your tone."
Uday stopped. He looked at the bag, then at his father. "Sorry. That was rude. May I explain why I want to go? Five minutes?"
"Five minutes."
"It's the group project, Papa. Four of us, at Farhan's house, till eight. His mother will be home. I'll text the moment I arrive and the moment I leave."
Gautam folded the paper. "What is the project?"
"Water saving in our colony. We present on Monday."
"Eight sharp, and you call me."
"Deal, Papa. Thank you."

qa.q: Until what time does Uday want to stay at Farhan's house?
qa.a: Uday wants to stay until eight.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling when he slammed the bag and said Papa had not listened?
qa.a: Uday felt frustrated and dismissed. The slammed bag shows that he was angry at being refused without a hearing.

qa.q: What did Uday change after his father said "Watch your tone", and why did it work?
qa.a: Uday apologised, asked "May I explain?" and gave clear details about who, where and when. That let his father listen and agree with a condition.

qa.q: What might Gautam have been thinking when Uday first shouted?
qa.a: Gautam may have felt disrespected and cautious about the plan. After the apology and details he felt reassured enough to say yes.

grounding: A teenager who argues with a father begins rudely, then uses respectful directness, "may I explain", and is heard.
